newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers absent in bearish market.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers absent in bearish market.

text.p: German chocolate manufacturers remained absent from weak cocoa bean markets where futures were pressured by strong sterling, traders said on Wednesday.
A stronger sterling, as a result of a quarter-point UK interest rate rise, raises chances of cocoa producer sales.
"There could be further liquidations on December and March," one Hamburg trader said.
"Consumers won't buy in a falling market...physical bean and butter differentials are also easing."

Traders said although arrival reports in West Africa did not yet allow firm clues as to the size and quality of the 1996/97 crop, there was no impression of tightness, which added to the bearish tone.
Local bean prices were 0.04 marks/kg down on the week at 2.23 marks/kg for Nov/Dec and at 2.27 marks for first quarter 1997, down 0.05.
The cocoa butter ratio eased to 2.79 from 2.84 previously for 1996 dates. Implied butter prices liquid ex-works at 6.38 marks were down 0.21 on the week.
